daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

NasDem party chairman Surya Paloh has proposed raising the parliamentary threshold to 7 percent, declaring his party would accept not entering parliament if such a rule were applied. Paloh also stated that the election law should be a priority and questioned why deliberations should wait until next year, while separately hearing proposals for a presidential nomination threshold requiring at least two parliamentary factions. Non-parliamentary parties have rejected the proposed 5 percent threshold, accusing the coalition of arrogance and obstruction.

  • PAN responded to party leader Zulkifli Hasan's decision not to run for president by reaffirming continued support for President Prabowo.
  • Golkar's secretary-general confirmed that Nusron Wahid resigned from party leadership six months ago.
  • President Prabowo cited his government's achievements after two years in office.
  • Surya Paloh commented on the proposed asset forfeiture bill, saying if urgent proceed but avoid creating controversy.
  • The KPK found evidence of fund flows in the ATR/BPN corruption case after searching the home of the director-general.
  • The Ministry of Public Works temporarily dismissed a civil servant who cultivated marijuana in Bandung.
  • Former West Java Governor Danny Setiawan passed away, as announced by current Governor Dedi Mulyadi.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia and the Netherlands will co-host the 2027 UN Peacekeeping Ministerial, reinforcing Indonesia's international peacekeeping role. The announcement came as President Prabowo shouted "Free Palestine" and was immediately embraced by the Palestinian ambassador at an event. Indonesia also leads ASEAN Committee in Washington to strengthen the bloc's voice in the United States.

  • Indonesia discussed Whoosh railway debt repayment during meetings in China.
  • Indonesia and Australia strengthened counter-terrorism collaboration through bilateral consultations.
  • Indonesia handed over an Ethiopian Interpol fugitive to Addis Ababa authorities.
  • The TNI is hunting OPM suspects after a driver was killed in Papua.
  • The Indonesian Army will inaugurate five new regional commands on October 5, which will feature in TNI's 81st anniversary celebrations alongside the KRI Garibaldi warship.

Other

Indonesia's tourism sector earned US$8.43 billion in the first half of 2026, marking significant revenue growth. President Prabowo separately affirmed food and energy self-reliance as essential to national strength. The government continues to face scrutiny over education costs, with PAN chairman Zulkifli Hasan revealing that independent pathway fees at state universities can reach Rp 100 million.

  • PTDI (Indonesian aerospace manufacturer) revealed plans to develop air ambulances for domestic medical services.
  • Basarnas kept helicopters ready as the search for KM Virgo Transport 8 victims entered day seven, with 12 elite divers deployed and nine victims identified by police.
  • The government will consider MSME conditions in implementing halal certification requirements.
  • Bogor authorities identified 23 companies suspected of polluting the Cileungsi River.
  • Agriculture Minister Amran's efforts to expose the fortified rice mafia received public appreciation, while a DPR member called on businesses to ensure nutritional content in fortified rice.
